messages:
Alex: Heads-up — surface-level alert: rack r12 in eu-west showed a big egress spike ~10m ago, causing latency regressions on a handful of dedicated slices. Seeing sustained egress >600Mbps from a single host.
Priya: ACK. Any tenant id or pod?
Alex: quick grep from proxy logs shows tenant=acme-analytics, host=rack-r12-03. snippet: `OUTBOUND_BYTES=6.2e8 duration_s=60 tenant=acme-analytics conn=20`
Jesse: ugh noisy neighbor. Is this spilling into co-located dedicated pools or just shared?
Alex: Primarily hitting the egress uplink on the rack, but the scheduler is reporting increased queueing for dedicated-slice workers on r12 -> those slices are getting 2-3x token latency.
Marta: Can we soft-quarantine the host or move the ACME tenant to a warmpool in another AZ? Cost will be higher but keeps SLAs.
Tom: We have soft-isolation rules but they trigger on packet-loss thresholds. This is pure throughput/persistent stream, so they didn't kick. I can bump the egress policer for that host to 250Mbps for now.
Priya: If we throttle host, ACME jobs will retry and may bump cost. Any rollback plan?
Jesse: Proposal: 1) throttle host to 250Mbps (Tom), 2) re-route new ACME allocations to eu-west-2 warmpool for 15m (alloc-bot), 3) mark host for postmortem and add a fingered metric for sustained egress per-tenant >300Mbps.
alloc-bot: reroute-request queued: tenant=acme-analytics target_pool=eu-west-2-warmpool duration=900s. status=pending
Tom: Throttle applied on rack-r12-03: `tc qdisc change dev eth0 root tbf rate 250mbit burst 32k latency 400ms`
Alex: Seeing ingress of latency regressions stop within 45s. :thumbsup:
Priya: alloc-bot, please confirm new allocations are landing in warmpool and not backfilled to r12.
alloc-bot: allocations rebalanced: moved 6 active allocs, new allocs pinned to eu-west-2-warmpool. fallback_policy=avoid_rack(r12)
Marta: We should add a cheap circuit: if tenant sustained egress >400Mbps on a node for 120s, escalate to hard-isolate (migrate) OR notify on-call. Low false-positive risk for analytics tenants.
Jesse: Agreed. Also log cost impact: migration + warmpool delta ~ $0.08/token-hour for that workload. We'll want to discuss on Monday whether to apply to enterprise tenants only.
Tom: I'll open a tiny PR to add the metric and a runbook entry.
Alex: filing quick incident note here and pinging ACME CSE to explain remediation.
Priya: thanks all. follow-up: check KV cache eviction on those slices after migration (kvcache eviction can spike w/ migration).
Alex: noted — I'll monitor and post updates.
